subject: neckties, brain blood flow and eye pressure
title: What If You Always Wore a Tie?

scenes.text: What if you always wore a tie? Your brain would notice before you do.
Within three minutes of tightening one, eye pressure rose in about seven out of ten healthy men tested.
Pulled to slight discomfort, a tight tie cut blood flow to the brain by about seven and a half percent.
Dizziness usually starts at around a ten percent drop, so most people would never feel a thing.
Meanwhile, ties rarely get washed. One hospital study found nearly half of doctors' ties carried potentially harmful bacteria.
So a tie won't hurt most people. It's just the one piece of office clothing designed to squeeze your neck.

description:
What if you always wore a tie? In a 2003 study, a tight necktie raised eye pressure within three minutes in about 70% of healthy men, and a 2018 MRI study of 30 young men found a tie tightened to slight discomfort cut brain blood flow by about 7.5%.
Symptoms generally start around a 10% drop, so most people won't notice; a 2004 hospital study found 47.6% of clinicians' ties carried potentially disease-causing bacteria.
